why_this_is_the_central_finding: Every gate defect found in this session was a way for a FORGED receipt to be admitted. This is the same failure one level upstream and already committed: the artifact that produces the receipt asserts that solvers ran and returned unsat, with no solver present. ClaimGate never caught it because ClaimGate validates receipt SHAPE, and the shape is impeccable. A gate that reads `ran: true` and a gate that reads a hand-typed `verdict: unsat` cannot tell either from a real run.
status_ladder_consequence: Numeric claims resting on these controllers are REPO-REPORTED DIAGNOSTIC ARTIFACTS. They are not `runs` for the solver or engine legs they name, because those legs were not invoked by the controller that reports them. Per CLAUDE.md the honest label is `exists`, and any downstream doc citing z3/cvc5/julia_z3 agreement from tower_g5 is citing a literal.
not_asserted_here: That the underlying result JSONs are wrong. They may have been produced by genuine runs at some earlier time; that is untested and is exactly the stale-artifact problem.
